input.summary: Full ledger built and traced. All 20 claims (device 1–10, system 11–15, method 16–20) were traced limitation by limitation to affirmative inventor passages: rigid base with first/second sides, motor coupled to the first side, air-extraction mechanism coupled to the first side and in fluid communication with a chamber on the second side, rigid low-friction loop/skirt at the perimeter of the second side (plastic, metal, PTFE, combination of rigid materials), non-sealing behaviour with air entering beneath the perimeter, continuous extraction maintaining sub-atmospheric chamber pressure, pressure-differential hold without operator downforce, all-rigid transmission path with less damping than a flexible suction cup, free sliding across areas while the vacuum maintains contact, guiding handles, rope/wire/cable pulling element with decoupled control, and — from the one affirmative USER passage on autonomous mode — small stirring elements whose vibration causes a constant forward motion. All 17 numerals (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48) were checked against the numerals table, the detailed description and every figure bullet; each denotes exactly one part in every appearance, each appears in at least one figure and in the description, and no numeral is used that is absent from the table. All six figure briefs and the Brief Description of the Drawings were compared part by part: the FIG. 1 part list, the FIG. 2 enumeration of sectioned versus elevation bodies, the FIG. 3 second side and perimeter member, the FIG. 4 bearing face / clearance / exposed face / bonding material / substrate stack, the FIG. 5 pulling-element embodiment with motor and extraction mechanism omitted, and the FIG. 6 single-body third embodiment with the covering element omitted all agree with the corresponding drawing paragraphs and with the detailed description. Section designations 2-2 and 4-4 carry the same repeated designation in the resulting view heading, in the FIG. 3 source-view brief (numeral 2 and numeral 4 at each end with arrows), and in the drawing description. Functional-surface geometry was examined specifically: the bearing face shape, perimeter-member depth and width, ring plan form, the extraction gap through the base, band depths, stirring-element number/form/position, and the pulling-element sweep width are each declared depiction conventions inside their briefs only, with no untraced statement of taper, angle, runout, deeper end, radial or circumferential position, or contact topology; the partial-contact / partial-clearance topology shown in FIG. 2 against FIG. 4 traces to the inventor's own "maintaining rigid contact with the tile" plus "removes air entering beneath the rigid perimeter", and the application text stays shape- and location-neutral, adding no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" broadening to justify a renderer choice. Claim and description relationships and terms match (perimeter member, bearing face, clearance, chamber, first/second side, exposed face, flexible pulling element, stirring element); antecedent basis and the "placed against / brought against" contact recitations are consistent across claims 1, 11 and 16. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction to a person, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in any application section; the bracketed prior-art reference tokens in the Background are the pipeline's citation markers for the separate citation review and are attached only to prior-art characterizations, which need no inventor support. No unsupported technical assertion, no numeral conflict, and no figure-to-text inconsistency was found.
